title: Ireland – Passenger information system – 9947 Station Services Mediation System (SSMS)
description: Iarnród Éireann – Irish Rail (IÉ) is seeking to establish a contract for the design, supply, configuration, integration, commissioning, support and maintenance of a Station Services Mediation System (SSMS). The SSMS will provide the central processing, integration and management platform for real-time passenger information services across the Iarnród Éireann railway network. The system will interface with existing and future IÉ operational systems, including timetable systems, signalling systems, Passenger Information Display Systems (PIDS), Long Line Public Address (LLPA) systems and external passenger information platforms. The solution will support the phased migration from IÉ's existing Customer Information Systems to the future Centralised Traffic Control and Communications Based Interlocking (CBI) environment while maintaining continuity of passenger information services throughout the transition. The scope includes all necessary software, licences, configuration and integration services, testing, commissioning, migration, documentation, training, maintenance, technical support, cybersecurity updates, lifecycle and obsolescence management required to provide a fully operational and supported SSMS solution. The proposed contract will be for an initial period of eight (8) years, with an option for IÉ to extend the contract for a further three (3) years at its discretion.

description: Objective of the assignment is to assist in formulating the fourth phase of the EU Anti-Corruption Initiative in Ukraine (EUACI IV). EUACI IV will be funded by the EU, Denmark, UK International Development and Germany. Method: The formulation will be conducted based on a combination of documentary reviews and interviews with key stakeholders. The formulation team will undertake a field mission to Ukraine – up to two weeks (incl. travel days) if applicable, including to one or two of six target cities (“Integrity Cities”). The security situation in Ukraine is unpredictable, and planning of the assignment has to be adaptive to changing circumstances. If travel is not possible the formulation will be desk based and interviews conducted online. Outputs: 1) An Inception Report prior to the mission to Ukraine. 2) A presentation of preliminary findings and an outline of the draft Program Document 3) A draft programme document for Early Appraisal and presentation to the External Panel. 4) A final Program Document. Timing: The Formulation is expected to start 23.11 2026 with the submission of the draft Programme document 08.01 2027. Finalisation of Programme document after Early Appraisal and presentation to the External Panel expected 24.03 2027. Consultancy team: Two external international experts and one national expert with proven experiences. These include: 1) Expert in programming and management, including financial management, and experience within good governance and anti-corruption (International). 2) Expert in anti-corruption programmes and institutions including with knowledge of emerging trends, e.g. digitalisation and prevention (International), preferably a practitioner or with an academic anti-corruption profile. 3) Expert on Ukrainian public sector reforms and strong knowledge of the national anti-corruption institutions and local authorities (National). The Service includes detailed programme planning, national and international participant scouting, marketing and communications, management of the application and selection processes, implementation of three (3) accelerator batches, participant-specific support, partner and investor engagement, monitoring, reporting and final handover. The Service is intended for Finnish and international startups, growth companies, research-based teams and potential spin-offs that have progressed beyond the initial idea stage. Tenders will be compared solely on the basis of quality, with a weight of 100%. One (1) Supplier will be selected. Tenderers may submit a tender individually or as a consortium. The selected Supplier shall be responsible for the performance of the Service in its entirety, including work performed by consortium members and subcontractors. title: IM/IT Research and Advisory Services
description: The NRC Chief Information Officer Branch (CIOB) requires Tier 1 – Executive level IM/IT Research and Advisory Services to enable its IT executives, managers, and technical staff to make informed, strategic, and operational decisions based on current industry and technological trends. These services include access to an electronic self-service platform that provides comprehensive resource materials, such as articles, reports, templates, blueprints, white papers, and strategic planning guides. title: Laboratory-Scale Gas Atomizer
description: The National Research Council of Canada (NRC) is seeking the supply, delivery, and installation of a laboratory-scale Gas Atomizer (GA) to enhance powder synthesis activities at the Clean Energy Innovation (CEI) facility in Mississauga. At the CEI-Mississauga facility, the development and production of advanced battery materials is one of the core activities. High-quality, spherical metal and alloy powders are crucial in advancing the research on energy materials. Obtaining powders with precise alloy compositions, particle sizes, morphologies, and quality in small quantities from commercial sources poses significant challenges. To address this issue, NRC intends to procure a GA capable of preparing molten alloys with specific compositions and atomizing them using high-speed gas to produce spherical and fine powders.

title: Purchase of one (1) General-Purpose Laboratory Vacuum Vessel
description: NRC’s Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Center performs cryogenic research to support its astronomical instrumentation program. To support the development of cryogenic instrumentation, it is beneficial to test mechanisms at cryogenic temperatures to verify their performance and lifetime. To enable this testing, NRC is building a test cryostat to allow custom and commercial cryogenic mechanisms to be tested thoroughly prior to use in an instrument. This vacuum vessel will be integrated with a cryocooler, vacuum pump, and other custom parts to create this new cryogenic testing capability.

title: HIGH THROUGHPUT SIMULTANEOUS DYNAMIC VAPOR SORPTION (DVS) ANALYSIS SYSTEM
description: Canada is seeking offers from Offerors to provide a high throughput simultaneous dynamic vapor sorption (DVS) analysis system to characterize and quantify the adsorption and desorption behavior of advanced materials, including CO2 capture sorbents exposed to CO2/N2/humidity gas mixtures, battery materials such as solid electrolytes, cathodes, and anodes, and catalysts used in hydrogen production and carbon conversion applications to the National Research Council Canada. title: Basin Dredging, Garnish, NL
description: The scope of work for this project consists of furnishing all labour, plant, equipment, materials, supervision and incidentals required for the Garnish Harbour Dredging Project at Garnish, Newfoundland and Labrador. In general, the work under this contract includes, but is not necessarily limited to, the following: 1. Harbour Dredging Works – Dredging of designated harbour areas to restore navigational depths and improve vessel access. 2. Removal of Underwater Obstructions – Removal and management of sediment, boulders, debris and other underwater obstructions encountered within the dredging limits. 3. Transportation and Disposal of Dredged Material – Loading, hauling and disposal of all dredged material at an approved waste management facility. 4. Marine Survey and Verification Services – Provision of survey and positioning services required to support dredging operations and confirm completion of the work. 5. Environmental Protection and Site Restoration – Implementation of environmental protection measures during construction, followed by site cleanup, restoration and demobilization upon completion of the project. The completion date for all work under this project must be completed 12 weeks after award date. Before submitting a bid, it is recommended that Contractors visit the site and its surroundings, at their own expense and schedule, to review and verify the form, nature and extent of the work, materials necessary for the completion of the works, the means of access to the site (including ferry services), severity, exposure and uncertainty of weather, soil conditions, any accommodations they may require, and in general shall obtain all necessary information as to risks, contingencies and other circumstances which may influence or affect their bid. No allowance shall be made subsequently in this connection on account of error or negligence to properly observe and determine the conditions that will apply. Take all appropriate safety measures for any visit to the site, either before or after acceptance of the bid.

title: Dredging - Admirals Beach, NL
description: TWO PHASE SELECTION PROCESS PHASE 1 - REQUEST FOR QUALIFICATION The scope of work for this project consists of furnishing all labour, plant, equipment, materials, supervision and incidentals required for the Dredging Admirals Beach Small Craft Harbour project at Admirals Beach, Newfoundland and Labrador. In general, the work under this contract includes, but is not necessarily limited to, the following: 1. Harbour Dredging Works – Dredging of the harbour basin and channel to restore navigational depths and improve marine access within the harbour. 2. Removal and Disposal of Dredged Material – Removal, transportation and disposal of dredged sediments, boulders, debris and other dredgable materials at approved upland disposal facilities. 3. Marine Survey and Dredging Control Services – Provision of marine survey services, dredging control and verification activities required to support the dredging operations and confirm completion of the work. 4. Environmental Protection Measures – Implementation and maintenance of environmental protection measures associated with marine construction activities, including measures to control sediment migration, protect fish habitat and prevent pollution of the surrounding marine environment. 5. Marine Operations and Harbour Coordination – Coordination of the work with harbour users and marine traffic, including the management of vessels, floating equipment and construction activities within the harbour environment. title: Science-Policy Frameworks for Nationally Coordinated, Place-Based Freshwater Macroplastics & Microplastics Monitoring in Canada
description: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) has a requirement to strengthen our existing understanding of effective, properly scoped, monitoring objectives for both macroplastics and microplastics via freshwater monitoring strategies; identify fit-for-purpose monitoring approaches aligned with relevant sources, pathways and distribution across key environmental compartments (surface water, sediment, biota); and consider feasibility within current analytical and operational constraints.
